baseline_incident_edges.relationship: Independent historical research and publishing: antebellum education (1915), the Journal of Negro History (1916), migration history (1918), and a critique of educational dependence (1933).
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: The 1919 education preface, 1918 migration preface/opening, and 1933 preface/chapter I were read. Pyne and the NPS supply institutional dates. Earlier Black historical organizations and community support preclude a sole-founder claim.

baseline_incident_edges.relationship: Negro History Week (1926) combines public historical education with the research and publishing programme supported by Black communities.
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: Pyne’s LOC essay describes the programme and community financing; the NPS reproduces Woodson’s public-education statement. This is a documented commemorative/educational practice predating the later professional label public history, not self-identification with that profession or sole invention of commemoration.

existing_claim_assessment: Preserve both field contributions and all five original source limits exactly; no sole-founder claim, no new chronology or biography.

coverage.resources: Own textbook recommendation in DuBois1935; family, oral testimony, Moorland, Jameson and academic training leads explicitly held for absent endpoints.

coverage.reception: Own Higginbotham2011 testimony distinguishes Brooks’s mediation and later reading; Franklin/Greene/Reddick absent-endpoint holds.
coverage.limits: Bounded selected readings; not exhaustive network. Most cited originals and interview recording unread.
